title: Spectroscopy of retained device memory under continuous batching with async-prefetch pool
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Long-running inference services (continuous batching + KV prefetch) report gradual device RSS growth over 24-72 hours. Growth reproduced on multiple instance types (A100-40GB, H100-80GB) but not visible in single-shot small-load tests. Growth appears correlated with high prefix reuse and prefetch windowing, where many small allocations are created and freed on streams that outlive work by a few hundred milliseconds. This ticket captures the investigation plan, experimental results, temporary mitigations, and proposed runtime changes to avoid slow-to-return resident pages and mini-slab retention that increase fragmentation and effective capacity loss.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy stress harness: continuous-batcher v2 with workload trace from prod-replay-2025-01 spanning 48h.
2) Enable KV prefetch with window=2048 tokens and async-prefetch (stream-per-request) on runtime node.
3) Run at 60% load and observe GPU RSS via nvidia-smi and /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/memory_resident periodically (1m cadence).
4) Collect allocator traces (jemalloc hooks + cudaMemPool APIs) and stream-timeline events with timestamps.
5) Compare to a control run with batching but prefetch disabled and single-global-prefetch-stream.
6) Capture kernel-level pinned allocations using pmap and os-level pinned page counts.
7) Run a deterministic microbenchmark that allocates many small KV slices and frees them from a delayed callback stream to validate delayed free hypothesis.
hypothesis: Memory is not leaking at the CUDA driver level but is being held resident due to delayed stream decommit semantics combined with multi-pool staging (pinned host staging + device slabs). Two possible contributing mechanisms: (A) cudaMallocAsync retains device pages in GPU arenas because frees happen on streams that remain active (stream-quarantine), preventing immediate device page return to OS; (B) our mini-slab allocator buckets small KV slices into many tiny slabs which fragment multipool arenas and prevent coalescing, meaning freed device pages remain physically resident even though logically free, causing long-tail RSS growth.
experiments: Experiment 1: Force synchronous frees on the completion stream (cudaDeviceSynchronize per N requests) and observe if RSS drops — expected fast drop if stream-quarantine is dominant.
Experiment 2: Switch allocator to 'large-slab-first' policy for KV objects (>8KB) to reduce mini-slab churn; run 72h baseline comparison.
Experiment 3: Use cudaMemPoolReturnToOs with different thresholds after free to test driver-side release behavior (on supported driver builds).
Experiment 4: Disable pinned host staging for prefetch path (use CPU copies) to measure impact on pinned page counts and fragmentation.
Experiment 5: Insert periodic cudaMallocAsync trimming pass (every 30s) to trigger pool compaction and observe RSS volatility and performance impact.
Experiment 6: Add per-stream allocation counters to detect if certain long-lived streams account for >90% of outstanding allocations.
temporary_mitigations: 1) Recommend reducing prefetch window from 2048 -> 1024 for high-P95 workloads until a fix lands.
2) Turn on 'prefetch_stream_pooling' feature flag: reuse a small set of streams for prefetches to avoid many ephemeral streams holding frees.
3) Deploy background trimming task on Dedicated nodes that runs cudaMemPoolTrim-like operations every 60s as an emergency measure.
4) Add operator alert when device RSS increases >12% over 6h with low compute utilization (possible ghost residency).
investigation_notes: 2025-02-19 - Rohan: Collected traces from two A100 nodes; observed that ~70% of small frees are issued on streams that remain 'active' for 300-700ms. Correlation between stream hold time and resident retention strong (Spearman 0.87).

2025-02-22 - Infra: Re-ran with driver 525.85 -> 535.54: minor improvement, but long-tail still present. Driver-level debug (NV_PROF) shows pool returns are batched by the driver and not immediately reflected in RSS.

2025-02-24 - Eng: Modified allocator to coalesce adjacent mini-slabs into 64KB super-slab when contiguous free segments present; test shows 15% reduction in resident fragmentation for the microbenchmark.
2025-02-26 - PM (Jordan Lee): Customer A reported app-level OOMs after 5 days; applied prefetch flag rollback and customer incidents stabilized within 2 hours.
2025-02-27 - Security: No sensitive data in traces; safe to attach limited allocator traces for offline review.

decisions: 1) Short term: enable prefetch_stream_pooling=true in prod for all heavy-KV tiers (agreed 2025-02-25).
2) Medium term: implement super-slab coalescer in runtime-1.21 as opt-in config (estimate 3 sprints).
3) Long term: collaborate with driver team to expose a finer-grained return-to-os control or advisory API, and track downstream kernel behavior in our test harness.
4) Rollout plan: Canary change for pooling -> monitored for 72h, then gradual ramp across Dedicated clusters.
5) Do not expose synchronous trimming as default because of potential P95 latency impact; keep as admin mitigation.
next_steps: A) Complete Experiment 1 & 3 on H100 fleet (Rohan) by 2025-03-04.
B) Merge super-slab coalescer behind feature flag and run canary on staging (Ava + Priya) 2025-03-06.
